verdict.rationale: Stripe Issuing's spending controls are its own declarative rules: they automatically decline authorizations by merchant category, country, merchant ID or card presence, and enforce per-authorization or monthly limits. Single-use agent cards are also automatically invalidated after use. Beyond those fixed actions, custom event-driven behavior requires developers to write their own logic behind the synchronous authorization webhook, which is a building block rather than a rules engine. Missing for 10: general-purpose rule definition across event types, configurable actions beyond decline/limit/invalidate, no-code or AI-native rule authoring, independent or hands-on corroboration.
